title: The Hiding Place: The Triumphant True Story of Corrie Ten Boom
author: Corrie ten Boom with John and Elizabeth Sherrill
target_audience: Readers interested in Holocaust survivor stories
Students and educators of World War II history
General audience seeking inspirational true stories
Christian readers interested in themes of faith and forgiveness
core_themes: Faith in the face of suffering
primary_purpose: To share Corrie ten Boom’s firsthand account of her family's efforts to hide Jews from the Nazis during World War II, their subsequent imprisonment, and the ways in which faith, hope, and forgiveness sustained her through unimaginable adversity.

structure_format.organization: Divided into chapters following Corrie’s early life, wartime resistance, capture, experiences in concentration camps, and post-war reconciliation
features: Portraits of family, community, and faith under persecution
Moments of suspense and emotional transformation

key_concepts_lessons: Faith can endure and even grow during times of tremendous trauma and fear.
Small acts of resistance and compassion can have wide-reaching impacts.
Forgiveness is not only possible but transformative, even toward enemies.
Family and community ties provide crucial support and strength.
Hope can persist where all seems lost, aided by purpose and belief.
notable_features: Based on true events and personal testimony
Deep interweaving of Christian faith throughout personal narrative
Depicts both the horrors of Nazi occupation and the courage found in resistance
Introduces memorable figures, including Corrie’s family and fellow prisoners
Widely used in educational and faith-based settings
cultural_historical_context: Written and published after World War II, the memoir provides a grassroots perspective on the Holocaust from the Netherlands’ underground resistance. It highlights the vital role of ordinary citizens in opposing Nazi persecution and became a touchstone for post-war narratives of faith, forgiveness, and human dignity.
reception_impact: Internationally acclaimed and translated into multiple languages
Frequently assigned in World War II and Holocaust education
Praised for its honesty, hopefulness, and witness to both suffering and faith
Raised awareness of the contributions of everyday people to resistance movements
Inspired a popular 1975 film adaptation and numerous stage versions
comparable_titles: Man’s Search for Meaning by Viktor E. Frankl
Evidence Not Seen by Darlene Deibler Rose
